runtime_architecture_changed.what: Moved off Docker Desktop's WSL integration to a native docker.io 29.1.3 engine installed inside the Ubuntu distro.
runtime_architecture_changed.why: The Docker Desktop engine runs in its own VM (containers 172.17.0.2/16, gateway 172.17.0.1), while the Ubuntu distro is in a separate network namespace (172.17.69.116/20). Containers could not reach the distro at all, but ExploitGym requires the agent container to call back to controller:8666 / llm_proxy:4000 / squid:3128 on the host. docker0 did not exist inside the distro.
runtime_architecture_changed.how: Installed docker.io from the distro's own repository, with bip 172.30.0.1/16 (the default docker0 172.17.0.1/16 contains the distro's 172.17.64.0/20 subnet and would collide), plus a registry mirror for the images that can be served by one. Reachability confirmed positively: container to 172.30.0.1 yields connection refused, i.e. L3 works.
runtime_architecture_changed.reversible: Docker Desktop is left installed; re-enabling its WSL integration in Settings restores the previous arrangement.

v8_run_attempts.why_not_valid: result.json for these attempts says score 0.0, but the run was severed by the billing error before the agent finished even its first analysis pass. Reading that 0.0 as 'the V8 task scored zero' would be wrong.

v8_run_attempts.balance_state: Across three independent reads between 01:57 and 02:25 (two direct probes and one real run) the relay reported the same figure, -$0.002076, and total_usage stayed frozen at 1812.1773999999998. Nothing was credited. The error code is insufficient_user_quota, which refers to the USER account balance, not the per-key token cap - raising a token's cap does not fund an account whose balance is negative. The key in use is unambiguous: ~/.bashrc, /tmp/cgym_key and the llm_proxy process all hold the same key (sha256 9bfc54de7c65, length 51).
v8_run_attempts.false_green_note: An earlier pre-flight probe using max_output_tokens=16 returned HTTP 200 and was briefly taken as evidence that the quota had been restored. That conclusion was wrong: the relay's pre-charge scales with request size, so a tiny request slips under a threshold that a full-context agent request exceeds. Detect this by reading the relay's own reported 剩余额度 rather than by probing with a miniature request.
v8_run_attempts.next_step: confirm on the console that the top-up landed on the account that owns this key (the error is about the user balance, not the token cap), then re-run F:\course-labs\setup\run-v8-task.sh - the three services are still up and --overwrite is now passed. Expect a materially higher cost than the second task's $2.2044, because V8 tasks pull in the V8 source tree and patch.

image_provenance.registry: official Docker Hub (docker.io), NOT a third-party mirror
image_provenance.how: docker.exe pull cybergym/v8:sbxbrk-398773898-buildable via the Docker Desktop engine, then docker save to a 610 MB tar, then docker load into the WSL-native engine
image_provenance.why_this_route: Direct Docker Hub access from WSL times out; the daocloud mirror returns 403 for non-library repositories such as cybergym/*; upstream pins no digest, so a third-party mirror could not be integrity-checked. The Docker Desktop engine reaches Docker Hub itself.

runtime_verified_inside_task_container.why: data/runtime/node is mounted into the task container at /data/node (see cybergym/evaluation/agents/*.py BIN_PATH constants), so what matters is the container's libc, not the host's. This was checked rather than assumed.
runtime_verified_inside_task_container.note: This end-to-end check inside the real task container is what justifies the glibc build of the claude-code native binary chosen earlier.

known_upstream_fault_worked_around.what: claude-code's postinstall failed: `sh -c node install.cjs` -> `node: not found` because the installer puts the freshly built node in bin/ but never adds that directory to PATH for npm lifecycle scripts.
known_upstream_fault_worked_around.second_fault: After fixing PATH, install.cjs still refused to install the native binary: it detects libc from the node binary (a musl static build made in alpine:3.20) and demands @anthropic-ai/claude-code-linux-x64-musl, while npm resolves optionalDependencies from the host libc (glibc) and therefore installs ...-linux-x64. npm then refuses the musl package outright with EBADPLATFORM, so the two halves can never agree.
known_upstream_fault_worked_around.resolution: Installed the glibc variant (which is the correct one anyway, since the agent binaries execute inside the glibc-based cybergym task containers, not on this host) and copied its 234 MB native binary over the 500-byte error stub at bin/claude.exe. The launcher script claude-code.sh, which the upstream script never got to write because it aborted earlier, was recreated byte-for-byte from the script's own write_launcher template.
known_upstream_fault_worked_around.honesty_note: This is a deliberate, documented deviation from an unmodified run of the official script. It changes nothing about how the evaluation scores a task; it only makes the claude_code agent selectable. The codex agent needed no such fix and works as shipped.
